items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: And Jay was the producer on that so you know he’s kind of the overseer on everything.

ctx.x: When you read the minutiae about certain recordings I’m amazed that like Al Jarreau song “Breaking Away” I was just reading the minutiae about this and you know they had eight keyboard players and two guitars and two basses and horns and recorded in three or four different studios. I don’t have a question there but it’s amazing.

Well different keyboard players on different songs so you know George Duke I’m sure played on some things and there’s a guy who played in Al’s band for a long time, Tom Canning, I’m sure he was playing. Probably David Foster. Who else? I’m not sure but you know, and then the guitar players would be Jay Graydon of course, who is the producer, an excellent guitar player. Steve Lukather played on some things. Probably maybe Larry Carlton or Greg Parker depending on what the song called for. But you know that’s kind…

Yeah he had a great thing going on with those rhythm guitars and a certain kind of effect on them was really distinctive. I understand he liked to start his studio sessions like at midnight or something.
